newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - SOUTH AFRICA - JUNE 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - SOUTH AFRICA - JUNE 10.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Individuals wishing to take money out of the country from next month will no longer need a tax certificate from the South African Revenue Service -- a move which will make it much easier for people to invest overseas.
- The Inkatha Freedom Party in KwaZulu-Natal rejected "outright" an African National Congress proposal that IFP leader Mangosuthu Buthelezi's status be elevated at national level.

- The U.S. commerce department has issued a preliminary finding that Iscor and Highveld Steel have been dumping steel plate in the U.S. market -- charging less to importers there than to South African consumers.

- Publishing group Times Media Ltd raised headline share earnings to 275 cents in the year to March from the previous year's 258 cents, bolstered by good performances from its core and niche publishing divisions.
- Johnnic's Ikageng share scheme was 784 percent oversubscribed on a public offer of 9.1 million shares to the black community.
- French President Jacques Chirac had obtained a ceasefire agreement between the warring parties in Congo, officials at the French presidential palace said.
- More than 1,300 new posts are needed in the justice department for it to be able to maintain law and order under the enormous burden created by the crime wave, the department said.

- Johnnic chairman Cyril Ramaphosa hailed the 600 million rand offer of 9.1 million shares to black, coloured and Asian investors as "a great achievement" that firmly entrenched balck economic empowerment on South African soil.
- South African Airways [SAA.CN] has total liabilities of about six billion rand, most of which could be taken over by the government to facilitate the airline's privatisation, sources said.
- Short-term insurers Auto & General lodged a complaint to the insurance industry ombudsman against the Short Term Insurance Action Group, a newly established independent rival organisation.

- The Rethabile group, which acquired a 20 percent stake in Alcatel Altech Telecomms last week, was now a serious contender for a 100 percent stake in Sun Air [SNAJ.CN] worth about 100 million rand, group chief executive Moss Ngwenya said.

- The share price of Coronation Holdings gained a further 150 cents on Monday to close at a high of 88.50 rand on speculation that the highly rated financial services group is poised to make yet another strategic acquisition, this time possibly in the Sage Group .
